window: entry run-day close; amc out at next open, bmo out 13:00 ET report day

names.reason: Arithmetic on the H2-weighted guide and weak retail-IDC peers points to Q3 revenue landing in line to slightly light and the FY revenue guide toward its low end, under a consensus near the top. That is the shape that drew -17% in August. But the stock has already lost 59% in five weeks on sector news, is a crowded short, and has a strategic holder in at four times the price, so a merely adequate print could just as well bring relief. Neither side reaches 65%, and Monday's market tape is a large unforecastable part of a window that ends at 13:00 ET.
names.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 revenue print at or above RMB3.0bn with the FY guide raised or reaffirmed at the top end, or a new large wholesale order or a CATL-backed funding or strategic plan in the release, would make the relief case dominant. A cut to the RMB11.5bn low end, with utilisation still falling, would make the downside case dominant.

names.reason: No mechanism clears the bar. My arithmetic points to a small revenue miss against a stale consensus, and the Q2 template (small miss, guide reaffirmed below consensus, -17%) points down. But the stock has already fallen 72% since that print, mostly on sector and policy news that the release cannot reverse. A crowded short in a washed-out, levered stub could turn an in-line print into a squeeze. The two cancel at about a coin flip, with a wide distribution.
names.what_would_flip_it: Either an equity or funding announcement or a FY revenue/capex guide cut (clearly down), or CATL-backed funding with a reaffirmed guide and rising wholesale utilization (clearly up).

names.reason: The deciding line is Solutions revenue and whether the FY guide and the Q4 breakeven hold, and no public trace shows which way Solutions went in Q3. The platform beat is already public and translates only weakly into revenue. The cost path makes a breakeven reaffirmation likely, but so far that has only been worth an in-line EBITDA. Nothing I found puts the direction at 65 or above.
names.what_would_flip_it: Q3 Solutions revenue up quarter on quarter with new bookings named, plus a reaffirmed FY revenue range and a Q4 EBITDA near zero, would make me lean clearly up. A Solutions decline beyond -5% YoY with a trimmed FY revenue range, or a reverse split announced with the release, would make me lean down.

names.reason: The pre-released GBV and transaction beat is public, and my rebuild of revenue from those KPIs lands only at to slightly above the guide, because Solutions, the majority line, is not in the KPIs and has been the weak spot. There is no dated, independent evidence on Solutions or SaaS for Q3, so I cannot say the price is behind on the deciding line. The probability stays well below the 65 threshold.
names.what_would_flip_it: Solutions revenue flat or up YoY with a reaffirmed or raised Q4 breakeven and FY revenue guide (long case), or Solutions down high single digits with a softened breakeven or a financing or reverse-split announcement (short case).

names.reason: The comparison base makes a worse SSS print than Q2 likely (my arithmetic: about -24% to -29% against -17.8%), and the stock fell 18.8% on the Q2 headline. But the stock is already at its low after a 29% slide into the date, the parent's funding removes the solvency shock, and the market is too thin for a 13:00 Monday price to say much. The lean does not reach 65.
names.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 system SSS better than about -20%, or management saying October SSS improved materially after the September marketing push. Either would read as the turnaround starting and could squeeze this thin float up.
names.unpriced: Possibly the size of the SSS deterioration. Nobody publishes an estimate, and the comparison is about 6-7 points harder than Q2's because of last year's subsidy peak. That is a mechanical worsening the holder base may not have computed. But the 29% slide into the print may already hold it, and I cannot show either way.

names.reason: Comps (Q3'25 system sales +12.8% on delivery subsidies), the industry read-across (Luckin SSS fell from -5.3% to -11.1% in Q3) and the stock's record (3 of 4 prints down, -18.8% on Q2) all lean down. But the stock has already fallen 14% in five days to its 52-week low at $1, turns over about $14k a day, and has no consensus I can verify. So I cannot show what the price does not hold, and the scored 13:00 ET print may be a single odd-lot trade. My lean is below the 65 bar.
names.what_would_flip_it: A sequential improvement in SSS or transactions in Q3 (better than Q2's -17.8%) plus a credible breakeven timeline or a parent take-private or recapitalisation announcement would turn a thin $1 stock sharply up.
names.unpriced: Possibly the size of the headline revenue miss against a stale, sparsely maintained consensus (Q2 missed it by 27%) on a print that laps a subsidy-inflated base. I cannot show that the price does not hold it: the stock has already fallen to its low into the date, and with ~$14k a day of turnover there is no informed marginal holder whose expectation I can read.

names.reason: The likely headline beat versus a stale single-analyst estimate gives a mild upward lean. But DLNG trades on its sanctions and balance-sheet tail, not on EPS, and nothing in that tail is new since the 3 Nov update. The window is a post-weekend opening print in a sharply falling market on a thin unit, so the edge is far below the 65 needed.
names.what_would_flip_it: Off-hire or a loss of hire on either Yamal vessel in Q3. Another possible flip is new sanctions language, such as failure to replace UK insurers before 1 Jan 2027 or an event-of-default risk, or a cut or withdrawal of the $0.05 distribution.
names.unpriced: Possibly the gap between likely Q3 EPS (~$0.39-0.43 on my arithmetic) and the stale single-analyst $0.34. It is small for a stock priced on tail risk rather than on quarterly earnings, and it is easily swamped by the weekend tape. No sanctions, financing or charter fact was found that the price does not already hold.

names.reason: The quarter's numbers are close to locked in by the charters, and the units trade on the sanctions disclosure, which I cannot read ahead of time. The slide into the print and the history of flat-to-up opens favour a small relief move, but the 3 November warning about replacing UK insurers from January 2027 could just as easily be repeated or made worse. That is below the 65 bar, with no mechanism I can date.
names.what_would_flip_it: A sanctions update saying non-UK insurers or service providers are secured for Yenisei River and Lena River, plus a renewed buyback, would make me a clear long. Language that Yamal Trade disputes the charters or that cover cannot be found would make me short.
names.unpriced: Possibly an overshoot: the price seems to carry a full sanctions tail while hire is still being paid and the EU's 21st package keeps a legacy-contract exemption to July 2027. But I cannot show that this release will close the gap inside the window, because the decisive item (whether replacement non-UK insurance is in place for 2027) is undisclosed and could go either way. So nothing I can name as clearly unpriced.

names.reason: The price is being driven by a holder liquidating deal stock into a $10-30k-a-day tape, not by the fundamentals the release will report. The release's likely content (cash well above market cap, runway helped by the royalty sale) is already public in substance and did not stop the slide when it was announced. I cannot tell whether the seller is finished, which is the variable that decides the window, so there is no direction I would bet on.
names.what_would_flip_it: A material new item in the release: a passed pancreatic interim, or a runway pushed well out into 2028 (up); or an ADS-ratio change, a going-concern line or a new financing (down).

names.reason: The financing and pipeline news that matters was released before the print (11-16 and 11-18), and the tape traded through both with continued selling. So the Q3 release is unlikely to reveal anything directional that the price lacks. The rest is overhang flow against oversold mean reversion in an illiquid ADS, which I cannot call to 65%.
names.what_would_flip_it: A runway extension into 2028, or a reported pass of the pancreatic interim, would lean long. An ADS-ratio or reverse-split announcement, or strategic-alternatives language, would lean short.
